_comment: Reference list for MANUAL cross-checks only: codes documented to support checkpoint/restart, with the mechanism and where it is documented. It is NOT used to flag entries or in any computation (the analysis is code-agnostic); hpc_analysis.restart_cross_check() lists matches when a committee member asks. Compiled 2026-10 from the codes' documentation; 'reference_type' says whether the reference is the code's own documentation ('official') or a secondary source still to verify ('secondary'); all are official, and 'verified' records when and against which manual each entry was checked (all 17 on 2026-10-26). Support can depend on version, calculation type and settings (e.g. whether restart files were written before the job stopped). Matching is case-insensitive on the code name with spaces and punctuation removed; 'aliases' map other names.

quantumespresso.name: Quantum ESPRESSO (pw.x)
quantumespresso.mechanism: restart_mode='restart' continues an interrupted run; works only if it stopped cleanly via max_seconds (set below the queue limit) or a prefix.EXIT file in outdir, and with the same number of processors and parallelisation

vasp.name: VASP
vasp.mechanism: ISTART=1 (constant cutoff) or 2 (constant basis) reads orbitals from WAVECAR, default 1 when WAVECAR exists; reverts to a fresh start if WAVECAR is missing or has a different number of bands/k-points; ISTART=3 also needs TMPCAR

gromacs.name: GROMACS
gromacs.mechanism: gmx mdrun writes state.cpt checkpoints (interval -cpt) and continues with -cpi state.cpt 'exactly as if there was no interruption'; -maxh stops after a set wall-clock time
gromacs.notes: Binary-identical continuation only with the same build, hardware and processor count (without GPUs); otherwise statistically equivalent.

lammps.name: LAMMPS
lammps.mechanism: restart N / write_restart write binary restart files; read_restart restores box, atoms and most settings ('*' in the name reads the latest); fixes, computes, variables, kspace and output settings must be re-specified
lammps.notes: Exact continuation needs the same executable and platform; different processor counts, fix shake/langevin and some pair styles give statistically similar rather than identical runs.

cp2k.name: CP2K
cp2k.mechanism: MD state (positions, velocities, cell, thermostat/barostat) in .restart files, restored via EXT_RESTART (RESTART_POS, RESTART_VEL, ...); wavefunctions in .wfn files via WFN_RESTART_FILE_NAME with SCF_GUESS RESTART
cp2k.notes: Wavefunction files are binary and tied to the CP2K version that wrote them.

namd.name: NAMD
namd.mechanism: restartname + restartfreq write restart files (binaryrestart default; restartsave keeps a series); continue with bincoordinates, binvelocities and, for periodic cells, extendedSystem (.xsc), setting firsttimestep
namd.notes: restart*/bin* options checked on the 3.0 configuration-parameters page; extendedSystem/firsttimestep usage from the official NAMD tutorial.

amber.name: Amber (sander / pmemd)
amber.mechanism: 'restrt' file written every ntwr MD steps and at the end of the run; continue with irest=1 and ntx=5 (reads coordinates, velocities and box)
amber.notes: Amber 2026 Reference Manual, section 23.6 'General minimization and dynamics parameters' (pp. 431-432, ntx/irest/ntwr). Older than Amber 20: ntx >= 4.

openfoam.name: OpenFOAM
openfoam.mechanism: fields written to time directories per writeControl/writeInterval in controlDict; startFrom latestTime continues from the most recent

wrf.name: WRF
wrf.mechanism: restart_interval (minutes, <= run length) writes wrfrst_d<domain>_<date>; continue with restart=.true. and the new start/end times, running only wrf.exe (no WPS or real.exe)

octopus.name: Octopus
octopus.mechanism: binary restart data (e.g. wavefunctions) in subdirectories of 'restart' (gs, td, ...); RestartOptions sets paths and what is read; RestartWrite/RestartWriteInterval/RestartWallTimePeriod control writing

gpaw.name: GPAW
gpaw.mechanism: .gpw files: calc.write('x.gpw') (mode='all' adds wavefunctions), or calc.attach(calc.write, n, 'x.gpw') every n SCF iterations; continue with GPAW('x.gpw') or restart('x.gpw')

nwchem.name: NWChem
nwchem.mechanism: RESTART directive reuses the run database (file_prefix.db) and its files, keeping the same file prefix; list only the unfinished tasks after it. Recommended when a job runs out of queue time

siesta.name: SIESTA
siesta.mechanism: positions and velocities saved to SystemLabel.XV every step (MD.UseSaveXV reads them); seamless MD continuation via SystemLabel.VERLET_RESTART / NOSE_RESTART / PR_RESTART / NPR_RESTART / ANNEAL_RESTART; DM.UseSaveDM (default true) reads the saved density matrix
siesta.notes: Without the *_RESTART file, MD 'restarts' by repeating the last step from XV, which the manual says is not a seamless continuation.

abinit.name: ABINIT
abinit.mechanism: restartxf = -1/-2/-3 restarts MD or structural optimisation from the HIST.nc file written every iteration (also for unfinished runs; only predictors without random numbers); irdwfk=1 / getwfk read earlier _WFK wavefunctions
abinit.notes: Positive restartxf values are deprecated since ABINIT v8 (older forum advice to use restartxf 1 no longer applies).

dlpoly.name: DL_POLY
dlpoly.mechanism: REVCON (configuration) and REVIVE (statistics) dumped every ndump steps (data_dump_frequency) and at the end; continue by copying REVCON to CONFIG and REVIVE to REVOLD and adding the restart directive to CONTROL; with close time / job time set, a run out of job time stops cleanly

cpmd.name: CPMD
cpmd.mechanism: RESTART [options] in &CPMD reads the binary RESTART file (MD: WAVEFUNCTION COORDINATES VELOCITIES, plus ACCUMULATORS and Nose options if used; LATEST reads the newest). Written at the end and at intervals set by STORE; RESTFILE keeps several
cpmd.notes: The CPMD consortium's manual for CPMD 4.3.0 (6 March 2024), section 11.7 'Restarts' and keyword RESTART; this link is a copy hosted by the University of Calgary (project site: http://www.cpmd.org/).

castep.name: CASTEP
castep.mechanism: checkpoint written to seedname.check; CONTINUATION : DEFAULT restarts from the end of the previous run (only a limited subset of parameters may change; not combinable with REUSE)
castep.notes: Page is the BIOVIA Materials Studio 2023 CASTEP help, hosted by the CASTEP group at TCM Cambridge.
